A review here starts where the journal's peer review stopped. Each one applies the same
[protocol](protocol.qmd) to one published paper: design,
measurement, model adequacy, internal consistency of the reported numbers, reporting-guideline
compliance, and whether the conclusions follow. Every numerical check is reproducible from the
code in the [repository](https://github.com/albertoalamia/articles_reviews). Authors are
contacted before a review is posted and their replies are added. The reviews criticise methods
and numbers, not the people who produced them.

**Science anyone can check.**

::: {#reviews}
:::

## Across reviews

```{r}
#| label: tbl-programme
#| echo: false

source(here::here("lib/quality_table.R"))
pt <- programme_table()
if (nrow(pt) == 0) {
  cat("No review is published yet; the first two are with their authors for reply.")
} else {
  knitr::kable(pt[, c("Paper", "Field", "Track", "Verdict", "Critical", "Major", "Minor", "Confirmed", "Inferred", "Needs data", "Worst domain")],
               format = "pipe", align = "llllrrrrrrl",
               caption = "Issue counts per published review, from the registry (protocol H2). Systematic and selected tracks are never pooled.")
}
```
